title: Cocharacter Cartan factorization over a complete DVR
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $\pi$ be a uniformizer, and let $K$ be its fraction field. Assume $A\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/(\pi^n)$ is bijective [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. An $A$-group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] with base $\operatorname{Spec}A$. A reductive $A$-group scheme here means a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $A$-group scheme with reductive geometric fibres: over every algebraically closed field a fibre is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Write $\mathbf G_{m,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. For an $A$-algebra $B$, $H(B)$ means $A$-scheme morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}B\to H$, with the induced group law. A cocharacter is an $A$-group homomorphism $\mathbf G_{m,A}\to H$. Let $H$ be a reductive $A$-group scheme. For every $g\in H(K)$ there exist $a,b\in H(A)$ and a cocharacter $\lambda:\mathbf G_{m,A}\to H$ such that $g=a\lambda_K(\pi)b$ in $H(K)$. There is no assumption that the residue field is perfect, finite or algebraically closed, and no splitness assumption on $H$.

source.place: WANTED locally; read author-hosted https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/papers/iwahori.pdf. Theorem 1.3, implication (1) to (3), printed pp.1, 6; Definition 3.4 and Lemma 3.6, printed pp.5-6. The complete-DVR cocharacter form, before the non-complete descent of Theorem 4.1.

proof.text: Put $k=A/(\pi)$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A[s,t]/(st-\pi)$ and $o=V(s,t)$. Give $X$ weights $(1,-1)$ and put $U=X\setminus\{o\}=D(s)\cup D(t)$. On $D(s)=\operatorname{Spec}A[s,s^{-1}]$ and $D(t)=\operatorname{Spec}A[t,t^{-1}]$, take the trivial right $H$-torsors with action only on the base. On their intersection, $\operatorname{Spec}K[s,s^{-1}]$, identify the fibre coordinates by $h_t=g h_s$. The inverse transition is multiplication by $g^{-1}$; these satisfy the cocycle identities. Apply [lem-galois-glue] to glue the schemes. The right $H$-actions and the left $\mathbf G_m$-actions agree on the overlap because left multiplication by $g$ commutes with right multiplication and $g$ is constant along the base action. They glue by the same uniqueness; the torsor identities and local triviality hold on both charts. Denote the resulting equivariant torsor by $P_g\to U$.

source.place: Section 2, Claim 1; Section 3.3, construction of rho_g before Lemma 3.6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-nodal-equivariant-torsor-extension] to $P_g$: its group is precisely the smooth affine finite-type reductive $A$-group in the hypotheses. Obtain an equivariant torsor $\widetilde P\to X$ with $\widetilde P|_U\simeq P_g$. Restrict to the branch $t=0$, which is $L=\operatorname{Spec}k[s]$ with weight $+1$. Let $T=\widetilde P|_o$. Compare $\widetilde P|_L$ with the constant torsor $L\times_kT$, on which the action is the diagonal of scaling on $L$ and the induced action on $T$. Their fibres at zero are equivariantly identified by the identity on $T$, so [lem-sfb-contracting-line-equivariant-torsor-rigidity] identifies the two torsors on $L$. At $s=1$ the first is trivial, since this point lies in $D(s)$ and the prescribed restriction is $P_g$. Thus $T$ has a $k$-point $p$. Right translation $h\mapsto ph$ trivializes $T$.

source.place: Lemma 3.6, proof of (2) implies (1), first paragraph, with the two branches interchanged.

proof.text: The action on the trivialized fibre $T$ determines $\lambda_0:\mathbf G_{m,k}\to H_k$ by $z\cdot p=p\lambda_0(z)$. Commutation with the right action gives $z\cdot(ph)=p\lambda_0(z)h$; the action identity gives $\lambda_0(zz\prime)=\lambda_0(z)\lambda_0(z\prime)$ on all test schemes. It is a morphism of schemes since it is the action on $p$ composed with the torsor trivialization. Apply [lem-sfb-complete-dvr-cocharacter-lifting] to lift it to $\lambda:\mathbf G_{m,A}\to H$. Define $P_\lambda=X\times_A H$ with $z\cdot(x,h)=(z\cdot x,\lambda(z)h)$. The chosen point $p$ gives an equivariant isomorphism $P_\lambda|_o\simeq T$. By [lem-sfb-nodal-equivariant-torsor-rigidity] this extends to an equivariant isomorphism $P_\lambda\simeq\widetilde P$. Both applications use the stipulated completeness of $A$ and smoothness and affineness of $H$; neither uses any property of the residue field.

source.place: Lemma 3.6, proof of (2) implies (1), second paragraph; Lemma 3.3.

proof.text: Here is the transition calculation, including its orientation. For the global fibre coordinate $h$ on $P_\lambda$, use $q_s=\lambda(s)^{-1}h$ on $D(s)$ and $q_t=\lambda(t)h$ on $D(t)$. These coordinates are invariant under $z$, because $s$ has weight $+1$, $t$ has weight $-1$ and $h$ transforms by $\lambda(z)$. On the overlap, $q_t=\lambda(t)\lambda(s)q_s=\lambda(\pi)q_s$, so $P_\lambda|_U$ has transition $\lambda_K(\pi)$. Invert the preceding isomorphism to get $P_g\simeq P_\lambda|_U$. A right $H$-equivariant map in either chart is left multiplication by a chart morphism to $H$. Base equivariance makes that morphism invariant under scaling; evaluating the equality $f(zs)=f(s)$ at $s=1$ (respectively $f(z^{-1}t)=f(t)$ at $t=1$) makes it the pullback of a point $c_s\in H(A)$ (respectively $c_t\in H(A)$). Compatibility with the two transitions is $c_tg=\lambda_K(\pi)c_s$. Hence $g=c_t^{-1}\lambda_K(\pi)c_s$. Take $a=c_t^{-1}$ and $b=c_s$.

source.place: Lemma 3.6, observations (A), (B) and conclusion; Section 2, final observations (A), (B).

lean.statement: theorem completeDvr_cocharacter_cartan (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] (pi : A) (hpi : Irreducible pi) [IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span ({pi} : Set A)) A] (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] (H : Grp (Over (Spec (.of A)))) [IsAffine H.X.left] [Smooth H.X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType H.X.hom] [QuasiCompact H.X.hom] (hred : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (f : A →+* Ω), ReductiveTorusCentralizer.IsReductive ((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom f))).mapGrp.obj H)) (g : (Spec (.of K)).asOver (Spec (.of A)) ⟶ H.X) : ∃ (a b : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of A))) ⟶ H.X) (lambda : Grp.mk ((Spec (.of (LaurentPolynomial A))).asOver (Spec (.of A))) ⟶ H) (t : (Spec (.of K)).asOver (Spec (.of A)) ⟶ (Spec (.of (LaurentPolynomial A))).asOver (Spec (.of A))), t.left = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (LaurentPolynomial.eval₂ (algebraMap A K) (Units.mk0 (algebraMap A K pi) ((map_ne_zero_iff (algebraMap A K) (IsFractionRing.injective A K)).mpr hpi.ne_zero)))) ∧ g = (toUnit ((Spec (.of K)).asOver (Spec (.of A))) ≫ a) * (t ≫ lambda.hom.hom) * (toUnit ((Spec (.of K)).asOver (Spec (.of A))) ≫ b)
